The test image shows a split soybean stem with:
- White/light-colored pith
- Dark black material (sclerotia?) embedded within the stem cavity
- Bleached, dried white stem exterior

Key candidates: White_Mold (black sclerotia in white stem) and Sudden_death_syndrome (white pith when cut).

Let me check reference images for each candidate class.

The test image shows a split soybean stem with:
- White/light-colored pith (not brown, rules out Brown Stem Rot)
- Distinct black sclerotia embedded within the stem cavity
- Bleached, dried white stem exterior

The black sclerotia inside the stem cavity is the hallmark diagnostic feature of White Mold. The KB confirms: "hard, black sclerotia resembling rodent droppings on or inside stems and pods" and "Characteristic black sclerotia embedded within white fluffy mold on stem lesions and inside the stem."

SDS also has white pith but lacks black sclerotia. Charcoal Rot has microsclerotia but they appear as gray speckling, not as the large distinct black bodies visible here.
